strings: Worn Parchments are fragmented ritual writings carried by cultists encamped around the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore. Gathered by scouts, these tattered scraps provide the first concrete clues identifying the sinister sect gathering in the ruins.

North along the mist-shrouded coast of Darkshore, dark spellcasters and their zealous followers have seized the ruined Tower of Althalaxx. The foot soldiers patrolling the grounds outside, known as Dark Strand Fanatics, carry scraps of worn parchment among their personal effects. While a single piece appears as nothing more than fragmented scribbles and esoteric symbols, piecing together multiple fragments reveals the presence of a previously unknown organization: the Cult of the Dark Strand.

Balthule Shadowstrike, a scout monitoring the tower from a nearby overlook, uses these gathered parchments to assess the threat for Delgren the Purifier and the sentinels in Auberdine. piecing the texts together confirms that the warlocks in the tower are not independent outcasts, but an organized coven working toward a calculated, malevolent objective.
The parchments are carried by Dark Strand Fanatics, the cultist foot soldiers encamped outside around the perimeter of the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore.

What is written on the parchments?
Individually, they are cryptic fragments of ritual notes and orders. Once gathered together and deciphered by Balthule Shadowstrike, they reveal the name and existence of the Cult of the Dark Strand.

Balthule was tasked by Delgren the Purifier to watch the Tower of Althalaxx. He needs the writings to decipher why warlocks have gathered at the ruins and assess the danger to Darkshore before reporting back.

What is the Cult of the Dark Strand?

They are a secretive gathering of cultists and warlocks operating out of the ruins of Althalaxx. Even seasoned scouts like Balthule Shadowstrike have never encountered their order before finding these writings.

The presence of dark spellcasters and demonic corruption near ancient ruins like Althalaxx is a severe desecration of Darkshore's sacred wilderness.

Worn Stone Tokens are small magical talismans carried by personnel and mages associated with Dalaran in the Alterac Mountains. Though their ambient magic has largely faded, they were crafted to help the Kirin Tor bind and command elemental servants.

The magi of Dalaran have long possessed a formidable command over elemental entities, using specialized talismans to bend these extradimensional beings to their will. Worn Stone Tokens represent depleted or exhausted versions of these implements. Carried not only by theurgists and summoners but even by Dalaran laborers and guards stationed around the ruins and internment camps of Alterac, they demonstrate how deeply elemental binding is integrated into Dalaran's everyday operations.

From their outpost in Tarren Mill, the Forsaken keep a watchful eye on the nearby wizards. Magus Voidglare sought specimens of these tokens to decipher Dalaran's methods of elemental enslavement. Keeper Bel'varil directs agents to collect worn, inert tokens first, allowing the Magus to safely analyze the foundational enchanting techniques before experimenting with more potent, volatile conduits.
What were these tokens used for?
Dalaran's wizards use these magical stone tokens to command and bind elementals summoned from other realms to serve as laborers, guards, and defenders.
worn stone token purpose | what are stone tokens | why do dalaran carry tokens
Why are the tokens described as worn?
Their active enchantments have faded over time and heavy use. Keeper Bel'varil considers these inert specimens safer for Magus Voidglare's initial research into Dalaran's binding rituals.
why worn | are tokens magical | inert tokens

They are found on various Dalaran personnel operating in the southern Alterac Mountains, ranging from high-ranking summoners and theurgists to ordinary laborers, shield guards, and Warden Belamoore at the internment camp.

Magus Voidglare wishes to study Dalaran's arcane techniques for controlling elementals, seeking to unravel the secrets behind their summoning and subjugation arts.

Mages recognize these tokens as the practical focus items the Kirin Tor uses to keep conjured elementals stable and obedient in the field.
Securing these tokens aids the Forsaken at Tarren Mill in studying the arcane defenses and practices of the hostile Kirin Tor presence in Alterac.

The Woven Wand is a unique enchanted relic crafted long ago by three Dalaran apprentice magi as a pledge of brotherhood. Following the fall of Lordaeron and bitter betrayals among its creators, the wand was hidden away in Fenris Keep before resurfacing in the hands of the Forsaken.

In the days when Dalaran still trained the young magi of the north, three aspiring wizards—Bethor Iceshard, Gunther Arcanus, and Thule Ravenclaw—intertwined their individual apprentice wands into a single talisman. This Woven Wand served as both a conduit of combined magical power and a symbol of their enduring friendship. That fellowship shattered irrevocably when the Scourge swept through Lordaeron. Thule Ravenclaw chose to swear fealty to the Lich King, turning to foul necromancy. Meanwhile, the Plague of Undeath claimed both Bethor and Gunther, eventually cutting their ties to Dalaran entirely.

Though Thule came to detest the sentimentality of the wand after turning to darkness, he could never bring himself to destroy it or surrender it to his former peers. Instead, he carried the artifact into Silverpine Forest and concealed it deep within an alcove in Fenris Keep. Decades later, with Thule's lair breached and his servant Alaric directing Horde agents to the hiding place, the relic was retrieved intact. Never having had its dormant enchantments invoked by the necromancer, the wand was finally delivered to Bethor Iceshard within the Magic Quarter of the Undercity.

The wand was crafted jointly by three Dalaran apprentice mages: Bethor Iceshard, Gunther Arcanus, and Thule Ravenclaw. They combined their three separate apprentice wands into one shared artifact to represent their friendship.
who made woven wand | creators of woven wand | wand creators
Why was the wand hidden in Fenris Keep?

After Thule betrayed his colleagues to serve the Lich King, he grew to despise the artifact and the bond it represented. However, he was unable to part with it or destroy it, so he hid it away within a secret niche in his lair at Fenris Keep.
why did thule hide the wand | where was woven wand found | why fenris keep
Why did Bethor Iceshard think the wand was lost?

Bethor assumed the wand had been permanently lost when their friendship collapsed and the plague ravaged the land. He also noted that Thule never dared to invoke its magical energies; had Thule used it, Bethor would have sensed the surge through their lingering magical link.

Horde adventurers assaulted Fenris Keep to defeat Thule Ravenclaw. Guided by the severed, still-talking head of Ravenclaw's former servant Alaric, they located the hidden niche containing the wand and brought it out of the ruins.

The Woven Wand illustrates the old traditions of Dalaran's apprentices, who often experimented with melding personal conduits to focus their collective arcane potential.
The artifact serves as a bittersweet reminder of mortal lives lost to the Scourge, uniting the memories of two Forsaken survivors against the madness of their fallen former peer.

A vial of pristine, magically infused water drawn from the base of the highest waterfall in the ancient elven ruins of Xavian. Horde mages in Orgrimmar seek it out to unravel the latent arcane powers preserved in Ashenvale's oldest sacred sites.

Before the Great Sundering, Xavian was a renowned elven settlement celebrated for its arcane scholars and ancient knowledge. Even after thousands of years of ruin and neglect, its waters are believed to retain potent magical properties. Deino, an arcane instructor in Orgrimmar, tasks rising mages with trekking deep into Ashenvale to collect a fresh sample straight from the pool below Xavian's tallest waterfall. Securing it requires braving dangerous territory, as the ruins are now fiercely guarded by corrupt satyrs hostile to any meddling spellcasters.
Where is the water sample collected?

It is gathered by filling Deino's Flask at the pool beneath the tallest waterfall within the ruins of Xavian. The site is located in northwestern Ashenvale, north past the lakes that lie beyond Splintertree Post and Satyrnaar.

Deino is an arcane instructor based in the Valley of Spirits in Orgrimmar. She studies potent and unusual sources of magic to educate young Horde practitioners, seeking the ancient magical essence preserved in Xavian's undisturbed waters.

The ancient elven ruins are inhabited by satyrs, demonic beings who hate intruders and fiercely defend their territory against curious mages. The surrounding waterways are also home to aggressive beasts such as river crocolisks.

As the Horde establishes a firmer presence in Ashenvale around Splintertree Post, harvesting the ancient arcane resources of Xavian provides vital knowledge for Orgrimmar's scholars.

Young Crocolisk Skin is a pliable reptile pelt harvested from juvenile crocolisks throughout the Wetlands. Prized by local tanners like James Halloran of Menethil Harbor, these softer hides are cured and exported to ports across Azeroth.
Tanning and Trade in the Marshes

Menethil Harbor serves as a bustling hub of commerce along the western coast of Khaz Modan, exporting marshland goods to distant ports. Among the town's most lucrative exports are the cured hides processed by the harbor's resident tanner, James Halloran. While full-grown crocolisks yield thick, tough scales, their young provide softer, far more workable leather. Because these juvenile skins are delicate and in high demand, Halloran relies on local hunters and passing travelers to scour the boggy marshes just outside town to keep his curing racks stocked.
Why does James Halloran want skins from young crocolisks specifically?

Young crocolisks yield significantly softer leather than their fully grown counterparts. While mature beasts possess thick, rigid scales, the hides of juveniles are far easier to work and cure into supple goods that are in high demand across sea trade routes.
why young crocolisk skin | halloran skins | why soft skins
Where can young crocolisks be found?
Young Wetlands Crocolisks inhabit the waterways, bogs, and marshes lying just outside Menethil Harbor in the western Wetlands.

A local hunter named Einar is known to regularly bring in crocolisk hides for James Halloran's leatherworking business, though demand often outpaces what a single tracker can supply.

Yowler's Paw is the grisly trophy taken from Yowler, the ferocious pack leader of the gnolls menacing the hills above Lakeshire. Brought to the town artisan Verner Osgood, it serves as undeniable proof that the beast leading the local gnoll packs has been put down.

The Redridge gnolls have long terrorized the heights surrounding Lake Everstill, their bloodcurdling howls echoing down into the settlement of Lakeshire. Among them, none is more feared than Yowler, the ruthless alpha driving their expansion. Because gnoll ears and paws are customary proof of bounties across the human territories, Verner Osgood asks brave adventurers to bring back Yowler's paw. Severing it marks not just the demise of an unusually cunning predator, but a deliberate move to shatter the chain of command among his disorganized followers.
A Town Left on Its Own

Bringing back Yowler's paw underscores the dire situation in Lakeshire. The Stormwind Army is completely consumed by the Blackrock orc threat entrenched around Stonewatch Keep, leaving civil authorities and townspeople to hire passing mercenaries for defense. In the absence of regular royal garrisons, securing proof like Yowler's paw is the only way settlers like Verner Osgood can ensure the local roads remain even marginally safe for trade and travel.
Verner Osgood, a prominent tradesman and resident in Lakeshire, requests the paw. He wants proof that the dangerous alpha gnoll terrorizing the hills has been permanently dealt with.
who wants yowlers paw | verner osgood paw quest | turn in yowlers paw

Yowler is the fierce leader of the Redridge gnoll packs. Unlike ordinary mongrel gnolls, he possesses the brute strength and cunning needed to rally multiple packs, making him an urgent danger to the nearby townsfolk.
who is yowler | yowler lore | redridge gnoll leader

The Stormwind Army is overwhelmed fighting the Blackrock orcs who have fortified Stonewatch Keep in eastern Redridge. With no reinforcements to spare, townsfolk like Verner Osgood must rely on freelance adventurers to hunt down threats like Yowler.

Slaying Yowler breaks the leadership holding the aggressive gnolls together, causing his pack to scatter into the wilderness and providing temporary breathing room for the residents of Lakeshire.

Defeating Yowler and recovering his paw helps stabilize Redridge Mountains at a time when Stormwind's military is stretched too thin to protect its own eastern frontier.

Zalazane's Head is the grim trophy brought to Master Gadrin to confirm the fall of the traitorous witch doctor Zalazane. Its retrieval marks a crucial step in freeing the Echo Isles from the dark magic holding the Darkspear tribe's home hostage.

When the witch doctor Zalazane betrayed the Darkspear tribe, he used mind-enslaving hexes to seize control of their island home, driving Vol'jin's people to the mainland shores of Durotar. From the Echo Isles, Zalazane continued to send hexed thralls across the waters to snatch more victims. To assure the anxious refugees in Sen'jin Village that the tyrant's reign of terror had broken, Master Gadrin demanded absolute physical proof of his demise. Returning the severed head not only confirms Zalazane's defeat in battle, but offers the displaced tribe a rare measure of peace and a hope of one day reclaiming their stolen islands.
Master Gadrin, the witch doctor residing in Sen'jin Village on the southern coast of Durotar, asks adventurers to bring him the head as proof that Zalazane has been slain.
who wants zalazane head | zalazane quest giver | gadrin zalazane

Zalazane was once a respected sorcerer among the Darkspear, but his lust for power led him to enslave his kin through mind-controlling magic. He drove the tribe out of the Echo Isles and continued raiding the mainland to capture more Darkspear for his thrall army.
why kill zalazane | what did zalazane do | zalazane lore
Zalazane resides on the largest of the Echo Isles off the southeastern coast of Durotar, surrounded by the hexed and voodoo trolls bound to his service.

For Darkspear trolls, claiming Zalazane's head is a deeply personal act of vengeance and justice against the traitor who drove their people into exile and enslaved their brothers.

Zamah's Note is a written dispatch sent from Zamah in Thunder Bluff across the Great Sea to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. It outlines an urgent request for an alchemical concoction capable of dealing with the Venture Company in the Stonetalon Mountains without relying on direct bloodshed.
A Plea Across the Great Sea

The goblin operations of the Venture Company have entrenched themselves deeply within the Stonetalon Mountains, deforesting and tearing up the sacred land. Zamah, seeking a specialized solution to dislodge them without inciting outright slaughter, turns to the expertise of the Forsaken Royal Apothecary Society. The note serves as formal correspondence detailing Stonetalon's dire situation to her colleague, Apothecary Lydon, stationed far away in Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills of Lordaeron.

Carrying the sealed message requires a long trek across continents, guiding Kalimdor travelers aboard zeppelins to the Undercity and down through Silverpine Forest into Hillsbrad. Upon receiving Zamah's dispatch, Lydon is immediately intrigued by her specific requirements, taking pride that word reached him from across the ocean and preparing to craft an alchemical answer to the goblin problem.
It is a sealed letter penned by Zamah in Thunder Bluff, addressed to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill, requesting an alchemical formula to remove the Venture Company from Stonetalon.

Zargh's Meats are a parcel of prime, raw cuts prepared by the orc Zargh at the Crossroads. Intended as a personal gift for Innkeeper Gryshka in Orgrimmar, they serve to introduce young Horde travelers to the regional wind rider network.

Prepared by Zargh, a butcher and hunter stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens, this package contains choice cuts of fresh meat destined for Gryshka, the innkeeper of the Valley of Strength in Orgrimmar. Because fresh game spoils quickly under the dry heat of the savannas, Zargh entrusts the parcel to couriers bound for the Crossroads roost. There, Wind Rider Master Devrak arranges swift aerial transit atop a wyvern directly to Orgrimmar's Skytower, sparing travelers an arduous overland trek through Durotar.

While ostensibly an ordinary delivery of provisions, the shipment carries a fond personal sentiment. Upon receiving the bundle, Gryshka readily notes Zargh's knack for winning a lady's favor through quality game, eagerly preparing to sear the rare cuts for her inn's patrons and guests. For newly arrived orc and troll adventurers, carrying the meats provides an essential introduction to long-distance flight transit between Kalimdor's Horde settlements.
The meat is gathered and packed by Zargh, an orc stationed at the Crossroads outpost in the Barrens.

Delivering Zargh's choice cuts to Gryshka introduces young orcs to their capital's heart in the Valley of Strength and teaches the necessity of aerial wyvern routes.

Zhevra Hooves are sturdy animal parts collected from the wild equines roaming the arid plains of the Barrens. They serve as hunting trophies brought to the Crossroads to prove a traveler's prowess against beasts far stronger than initial appearances suggest.

Zhevras may appear to be simple striped grazers, but their compact, muscular legs carry considerable lethality. Sergra Darkthorn, an experienced hunter stationed at the Crossroads, tests aspiring Horde scouts by sending them to harvest hooves from zhevra runners. The exercise is designed to hone a fledgling hunter's instincts and resilience, as a solid kick from a panicked runner is known to knock even a sturdy tauren flat on their haunches. Presenting intact hooves confirms that a hunter can handle swift, kicking quarry before moving on to Kalimdor's deadliest predators.
Sergra Darkthorn, an orc huntress located at the Crossroads in the Barrens, asks hunters to bring her four Zhevra Hooves to prove their readiness for tougher game.
